issues.failure_explanation: As written, the defining condition imposes the left derivative at t_{n-1} to equal w'(t_n). But the integrated representation gives (Pcal w)'(t)=Ptilde_{p_n-1}(w')(t) on I_n, and the right-endpoint interpolation property of Ptilde gives (Pcal w)'(t_n^-)=w'(t_n). For n>=2 the left limit at t_{n-1} from I_{n-1} is instead w'(t_{n-1}), so the printed condition would force w'(t_{n-1})=w'(t_n) for general w. The later cancellation at t_n in the useful-property identity and the initial-derivative bounds use the t_n condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the endpoint derivative condition in the two defining displays of \Pcalpbftt from (\Pcalpbftt w)'(t_{n-1}^-)=w'(t_n) to (\Pcalpbftt w)'(t_n^-)=w'(t_n); the orthogonality and value conditions are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The integrated Thomee operator is defined by endpoint conditions incompatible with its own integrated representation; without the index correction, the endpoint cancellation behind Lemma lem:added-1 and the subsequent a priori estimates for xi_h, rho, and e_h are not the ones justified by the source.
issues.title: Integrated Thomee operator endpoint derivative condition has an off-by-one interval index
issues.why_classification: A single index repair restores consistency with relation:SS-Ptilde and preserves every downstream rate and conclusion; no new lemma or loss of regime is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: After the inverse inequality the left side carries coefficient 1/[512 p_m^2(2p_m+1)] in front of S_m^2. To absorb 2( sum_n ||Pi_{p-1}f||_{L^1(I_n)} ) S_m by Young's inequality, one must take epsilon=mu_m=1/[1028 p_m^2(2p_m+1)]. The printed epsilon=1028 p_m^2(2p_m+1)=mu_m^{-1} would add a much larger multiple of S_m^2 and cannot be absorbed; the displayed final stability estimate does not follow as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use epsilon=mu_m=1/[1028 p_m^2(2p_m+1)] in 2ab<=epsilon a^2+b^2/epsilon. Since 1/512-1/1028=(129/128)mu_m>=mu_m, the stated bound with mu_m follows after weakening the leftover coefficient.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the constant-free stability estimate is invalid at the Young step; the stability statement itself is still recoverable with the corrected epsilon, and the a priori results that cite it are repaired by the same local correction.
issues.title: Stability proof applies Young's inequality with the reciprocal absorption parameter
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-constant correction in the Young inequality; the theorem statement, constants' scaling, and all dependent a priori estimates survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The bounds Wihler-1 and Wihler-3 are stated for v_tau in C^0(0,T;X) with v_tau|_{I_n} in P_{p_n}(I_n;X). In the reliability proof they are applied to Delta u_tau, i.e. with X=L^2(Omega), and the estimator contains nodal jumps of (Delta u_tau)' in L^2. The stated convexity assumption gives Delta u_tau in L^2(0,T;L^2(Omega)) at most, and the sufficient regularity for u gives u in L^infinity(H^2) and u' in L^infinity(H^1); it does not give L^2-valued nodal jumps of (Delta u_tau)' or Delta u_1 in L^2 when u_1 is only in H^1_0. Thus the reconstruction estimates are used outside their hypotheses and some estimator terms are not guaranteed finite.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add explicit hypotheses that Delta u_tau is C^0 in time, piecewise P_{p_n}(I_n;L^2(Omega)), and has L^2-valued nodal jumps of its first time derivative (in particular Delta u_1 in L^2), or restrict the semi-discrete solution to a spatial discretization for which this holds; otherwise replace those L^2 jump terms by negative-norm analogues as suggested in remark:negative-norms.
issues.overall_effect: The computable L^2 nodal Laplacian-jump part of the estimator, and therefore the constant-free L^infinity(L^2) reliability bound, is not supported for the semi-discrete space as stated unless extra spatial/time regularity of Delta u_tau is imposed or the jump terms are replaced by negative-norm quantities.
issues.title: A posteriori proof applies Wihler reconstruction bounds to Delta u_tau outside their regularity hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The reliability theorem can survive, but only after a contained strengthening of regularity hypotheses or a change of the jump terms; the advertised sufficient conditions no longer by themselves make every estimator term finite, while the main L^infinity(L^2) reliability structure is preserved.
